An inscription records thc restoration bf the temple of Proserpine by Cheriston, freed-man of Augustus and   procurator of Malta. Diodorus Siculus (L. C, 4) speaks of the importance and ornamentation of Maltese dwcllings, and to this remains of palaces   and dwellings of the Roman   period indicate a high degree of civilization and wealth. When forced to select place of exile, Cicero was X i. 8, 9) attracted to Malta, over which he had ruled as quaes tor 75 B.C. Among his Maltese friends were Aulus Licinius and Diodorus. Lucius Castricius is mentioned as a Roman govcrnor under Augustus. Publius was chief of the island " when St Paul was shipwrecked (Acts xxvii. 7); and is said to have bccome the first Christian bishop of Malta. The site where the cathedral at Notabile now stands is reputed to have bcen the residence óf Publius and to have been converted by him into thc first Christian   place of   worship, which was rebuilt in Io9ó by Count Roger, the Norman conqueror of Malta. The Maltese catacombs are strikingly similar to those of Rome, and were likewise used as places of burial and-of in time of persccution. Under the will of Corradino representalive of the blood of Roger the Normán, Peter of Aragon claimed  the succession, came to him by the revolulion known as " the Sicilian Vespers when 28,000 French were exterminated in Sicily . Charles held Malta for two years longer, whén the Aragonese fleet met the French óff Malta, and finally crushed them in the Grand Harbour. In 1427 the Turks raided Malta and Gozo, carricd many 'of the inhabitants into captivity, bvt gained no foothold. The Maltese joined thc Spaniards in a disastrous raid against Gerbi on the Alrican coast in 1432. In 1492 the Aragonese expclled the Jews. Dissatis faction arose under Aragonese rule from the periodical grants of Malla, as a marquisate or countship, to great officers of state illegitimate descendants of the sovcreign. Exemption was obtained from these incidences of feudalism by large payments to the Crown in return forcharters covenanting that Malta should for ever be administered undcr the royal exchequer without the intervention of intermediary feudal lords.
